title: Scalar projection formula and the Tor bound for an open immersion
statement:
Let $k$ be a separably closed field, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, $A$ a
finite commutative $\ell$-primary ring, and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ an open
immersion of finite-type $k$-schemes. Let $d\ge\operatorname{cd}(j)$
([def-kun-cd]; finite by [lem-kun-0f10]). Let
$K\in D(U_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ have Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ in the sense of
[def-kun-tor-amplitude]: $\mathcal H^r(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_AN)=0$ for
$r\notin[a,b]$ and every $A$-module sheaf $N$ on $U_{\mathrm{ét}}$. Then:

1. for every $A$-module $M$, with constant sheaves $\underline M_X$,
   $\underline M_U=j^*\underline M_X$, the projection morphism

   $$
   (Rj_*K)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_A\underline M_X\longrightarrow
   Rj_*\bigl(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_A\underline M_U\bigr)
   $$

   is an isomorphism in $D(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$;
2. $Rj_*K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b+d]$ on $X_{\mathrm{ét}}$;
3. $Rj_{\mathrm{proét},*}\nu_U^*K\cong\nu_X^*Rj_*K$ has Tor amplitude in
   $[a,b+d]$ against every module sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$.

Here schemes over $k$ are as in [def-weil-scheme-over-base] and finite type is as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], open immersions as in [def-weil-open-immersion], and separable closedness as in [def-kun-separably-closed]. Use the ordinary module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], the constant sheaf functor [def-kun-constant-sheaf], ordinary uncompleted derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor], and the projection morphism [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. The morphisms $\nu_U,\nu_X$ are the comparison morphisms [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]; pro-étale Tor amplitude means the all-module-sheaf test [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. The interval endpoints $a,b$ are integers and $d$ is a nonnegative integer. For an empty interval, on either site the Tor-amplitude assertion means the same displayed vanishing test in every degree; in particular the zero object satisfies it. This extends the nonempty-interval convention of [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude] without imposing an extra inequality on $a,b$.

proof.text: Test the Tor hypothesis with the tensor unit $\underline A_U$: $K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}\underline A_U\cong K$, so $\mathcal H^q(K)=0$ outside $[a,b]$. If $a>b$, all these sheaves vanish, hence $K=0$ and all three conclusions hold for the zero object. We henceforth have $a\le b$.

The finite-type schemes $X,U$ are Noetherian: apply finite type over a Noetherian base to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ (a field has just the ideals $0,k$). They are quasi-compact, and are quasi-separated by the locally Noetherian criterion. Every open subscheme of a Noetherian scheme is Noetherian; thus the inverse image in $U$ of each affine open of $X$ is quasi-compact. Consequently $j$ is quasi-compact. Its diagonal is an isomorphism since $j$ is a monomorphism, so $j$ is quasi-separated. Test on a basis of affine étale $V\to X$ factoring through an affine open of $X$, with the first arrow of finite presentation. These form a basis by the local definition of étale morphisms and affine open coverings. Write $W\subseteq X$ for that affine open. For any affine open $T\subseteq X$, the open $W\cap T\subseteq W$ is quasi-compact because $X$ is Noetherian. Cover it by finitely many distinguished opens $D(f_i)$ of $W$. Their inverse images in the affine $V$ are the distinguished opens $D(f_i|_V)$, hence are quasi-compact; their finite union is $V\times_XT$. Thus $V\to X$ is quasi-compact. By the étale finite-presentation lemma $V$ is of finite type over $k$. Its open subscheme $V_U=V\times_XU$ is Noetherian and quasi-compact; its inclusion in $V$ is a quasi-compact open immersion, hence of finite type. Thus $V_U$ is also of finite type over $k$ (on affine charts, composing finite lists of algebra generators again gives a finite list). Both $V$ and $V_U$ are qcqs and have finite torsion étale cohomological dimension by clause (2) of the finite-cd theorem. Clause (1) also gives finiteness of $\operatorname{cd}(j)$.

source.place: Clause (1), finite-type and finite-cd hypotheses for the testing objects

proof.text: We first record the cohomological bound, without tensoring. For any $E\in D(U_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ concentrated in $[a,b]$, apply the truncation spectral sequence to $j_*$. The module-sheaf categories on small representatives of these sites are Grothendieck abelian. A bounded-below injective representative is available, as required by that spectral sequence. Forgetting $A$-modules to abelian sheaves commutes with bounded-below derived direct image. Since $A$ is killed by a power of $\ell$, each underlying cohomology sheaf is torsion. The definition of $d\ge\operatorname{cd}(j)$ therefore gives $R^pj_*\mathcal H^q(E)=0$ for $p>d$. The spectral sequence is $E_2^{p,q}=R^pj_*\mathcal H^q(E)\Rightarrow\mathcal H^{p+q}(Rj_*E)$; its finite, exhaustive, separated filtration has associated graded $E_\infty^{p,q}$. Nonzero entries can occur only for $0\le p\le d$ and $a\le q\le b$, so every associated graded in total degree outside $[a,b+d]$ is zero. A finite filtration with all its successive quotients zero has zero underlying object, giving $Rj_*E\in D^{[a,b+d]}$. In particular this applies to $K$.

source.place: Clause (2), truncation argument made explicit by its existing spectral sequence

proof.text:
For a testing object $V$ as in step 2, write $V_U=V\times_XU$. The localized étale site at $V$ is the small étale site of $V$; the equivalence extends to constant $A$-module sheaves by using on each corresponding object the identical abelian group and scalar endomorphisms. Restriction of a K-injective module complex to a localized ringed site is K-injective. Also $j_*$ sends K-injective complexes to K-injective complexes: its left adjoint $j^*$ on constant-coefficient modules is exact. Thus if $I$ is a K-injective representative of any $E\in D(U_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$, both sides of the natural comparison
$$\lambda_E:R\Gamma(V,Rj_*E)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(V_U,E|_{V_U})$$
are computed by the identical complex $\Gamma(V,j_*I)=\Gamma(V_U,I)$. More generally, for every étale $W\to V$, the equality $(j_*I)|_V(W)=I(W\times_XU)=j_{V,*}(I|_{V_U})(W)$ identifies the complexes $(j_*I)|_V$ and $j_{V,*}(I|_{V_U})$ section by section. Since both $I|_{V_U}$ and $(j_*I)|_V$ are K-injective, this also identifies $(Rj_*E)|_V$ with $Rj_{V,*}(E|_{V_U})$. The sheaf counits on both sides send a section on $W\times_XU$ to its restriction on the same object; hence they coincide under these identities. Computing the derived adjunction on these K-injective models gives the same counits. Thus $\lambda$ is natural and identifies the counit of the composite right adjoint with the composite of counits. Restriction of derived tensor agrees with derived tensor of restrictions by the ringed-topos derived tensor pullback theorem, since slice restriction is exact. These observations apply to unbounded $E$; no boundedness of a tensor with an arbitrary module is being presumed.

source.place: Tags 08FI (lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open), 0D6H (lemma-Leray-unbounded), 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); explicit computation on the cited K-injective models

proof.text:
Put $P_V(E,M)=\mathrm{PF}_{V,A}(E,M)$ for the scalar projection map, and let $p=\mathrm{PF}_j(K,\underline M_X)$ be the projection map in the statement. The canonical maps satisfy
$$\lambda_{K\otimes^{\mathbf L}\underline M_U}\circ R\Gamma(V,p)\circ P_V((Rj_*K)|_V,M)=P_{V_U}(K|_{V_U},M)\circ(\lambda_K\otimes1_M).$$
Use step 4 to identify $(Rj_*K)|_V$ with $Rj_{V,*}(K|_{V_U})$, and write $K$ for its restriction in the following calculation. Restricting the defining adjunct of $p$ gives the adjunct for $j_V$: the counits agree by step 4, and restriction of the tensor comparison is the tensor comparison on the localized site. Here is the adjunction calculation establishing equality of arrows. On the localized sites write $c_V^*$ for the constant-complex functor, $J^*$ for restriction along $j_V:V_U\hookrightarrow V$, and $c_{V_U}^*=J^*c_V^*$. Their right adjoints are $R\Gamma(V,-)$, $Rj_{V,*}$, and $R\Gamma(V_U,-)$, respectively. Under $\lambda$, the counit for the composite left adjoint $J^*c_V^*$ is
$$\varepsilon^{c_{V_U}}_K=\varepsilon^J_K\circ J^*\varepsilon^{c_V}_{Rj_{V,*}K}.$$
By the two definitions of projection morphisms, taking the adjunct of either side of the displayed equality gives this same composite tensored with $1_{c_{V_U}^*M}$, preceded by the same pullback tensor comparison. Indeed the left side first uses $\varepsilon^{c_V}$ and then $\varepsilon^J$, while the right side uses their displayed composite. The comparisons for $J^*c_V^*$ and for $J^*$ after $c_V^*$ agree: on K-flat representatives their ordinary constant-presheaf comparisons have identity components, and restriction leaves each sectionwise tensor $s\otimes m$ unchanged; sheafification and localization therefore give identical derived comparisons. Naturality now moves the two counits past these comparisons, and the adjunction triangle identities cancel the inserted unit-counit pairs. Hence the adjuncts, and therefore the arrows, agree. This supplies the compatibility assertion needed in the blueprint's chain of isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map); formal composed-counit calculation for the scalar adjunction

proof.text: Apply the scalar projection theorem on $V$ to $((Rj_*K)|_V,M)$ and on $V_U$ to $(K|_{V_U},M)$. Its hypotheses hold by step 2 and because $A$ is a torsion ring. It permits arbitrary derived objects and arbitrary modules, so no finite presentation of $M$ or finite projective dimension is assumed. Both maps $P_V,P_{V_U}$ in step 5 are isomorphisms. The comparisons $\lambda$ are isomorphisms by step 4. The equality of step 5 therefore shows that $R\Gamma(V,p)$ is an isomorphism for every testing $V$.

These tests detect $p$ even when its source has not yet been proved bounded below. To see this explicitly, take an arbitrary K-injective representative $I$ of its cone $C$. Slice restriction is K-injective, so $H^n(V,C)=H^n(I(V))$. The presheaf $V\mapsto H^n(I(V))$ is the sectionwise kernel of $d^n$ modulo the sectionwise image of $d^{n-1}$. Exact sheafification identifies its associated sheaf with $\ker d^n_I/\operatorname{im}d^{n-1}_I=\mathcal H^n(C)$. Step 6 makes the presheaf zero on the testing basis. Every object has a covering by basis objects, so its associated sheaf is zero. Hence every $\mathcal H^n(C)$ vanishes and the cohomology criterion for the unbounded derived category makes $C=0$ and $p$ invertible. This proves clause (1).

source.place: Tag 0BKV (lemma-sheafification-cohomology), the kernel/image calculation from its proof

proof.text: For any $A$-module $M$ put $E_M=K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}\underline M_U$. By the Tor hypothesis $E_M$ has cohomology in $[a,b]$, so step 3 gives $Rj_*E_M$ in $[a,b+d]$. Clause (1) identifies it with $Q\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}\underline M_X$, where $Q=Rj_*K$. Thus every constant-module test of $Q$ has cohomology in $[a,b+d]$.

source.place: Clause (2), constant-module tests after the projection formula

proof.text:
Fix a geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$. A derived stalk is pullback to that point, and pullback is compatible with derived tensor. Stalks commute with cohomology, and the stalk of a constant sheaf $\underline M_X$ is $M$. Step 8 therefore gives
$$H^r(Q_{\bar x}\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M)=0\quad(r\notin[a,b+d])$$
for every $A$-module $M$. For an arbitrary sheaf $N$ of $A$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{ét}}$, take the particular module $M=N_{\bar x}$ separately at each geometric point. The same derived-tensor comparison gives
$$(Q\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N)_{\bar x}\cong Q_{\bar x}\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N_{\bar x},$$
so $\mathcal H^r(Q\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N)$ has zero stalks for $r\notin[a,b+d]$. Conservativity of geometric stalks applied to the map from this abelian sheaf to zero makes it zero. This proves the all-module-sheaf Tor bound of clause (2), with no constructibility assumption on $K,N$ and without asserting that geometric stalks are conservative on the pro-étale site.

source.place: Clause (2), passage from constant tests to arbitrary sheaves by geometric stalks
Clause (3), bounded-below direct-image comparison and all-sheaf Tor-interval comparison
